output.name: Skenal

anatomy.part: the lantern at the masthead, centred in the small lantern shape at the top of the mast
the tip of the pennant streaming from the masthead
the head of the sail, top corner, left of the mast
the foot of the sail, where the mast meets the top of the stern post
the stern of the hull, the back end of the deck
the keel, lowest point of the hull's belly
the bow, the front end of the deck

output.myth: A boat went out past the Leeward edge in the year the herring failed. Her name was painted on the stern in old red, and the sea took the paint before it took the boat. When the crew came home without her, the mothers scraped the name off the broken hull and burned the wood, so it would not be called. But a boat with no name cannot find its way home, and a lantern that cannot say what it is will hang wherever it is put. So it went looking. Aun saw it first, flying too low over the water. Ennu laughed and said it was welcome to any name it liked. Kael has cast for it many times and never caught it; the light always sits just above the rope. Sil watches it while she hunts her brother. If a lamp hangs too still past the reef, do not shout. Ask it, quietly, what it was called.
output.verse:
A lamp with no name
it drifts through the Vel, searching
ask what it was called

guess: A small sailing boat on choppy water, with a curved hull and a tall sail or mast
